Hey guy's figured I'd throw in some content since this subverse is lacking.

I bought my T450s about 2 months ago. I bought a customized one with the i5 5300u proccessor, 4gb RAM, 1080p non-touch display, 500gb HDD, non-backlit keyboard and no camera. Upon arrival I upgrade the RAM with a 8gb stick to bring it up to 12gb, added a 42mm 128gb m.2 drive, 6 cell battery, and promptly installed Arch Linux.

I was just going to use Windows 10 for the first night or so, give it a test run as I won't install it on my desktop for privacy reasons. Within 20 minutes it was running very rough, the desktop wasn't displaying properly, Window's explorer wasn't responding. Rebooting it just made it worse. So I just said screw it and installed the SSD, RAM, and Arch. Opening up the laptop was a bit of a pain, but I've opened my fair share of plastic latches and had it opened within in a few minutes. Upgrading the RAM and SSD was simple, the slots were easily accessible, and everything fit just right. The arch install process went very smooth (3rd time installing Arch), I didn't have any driver issues.

Since installing Arch and running for a few months now. I haven't had any hickups from the device. The keyboard feels solid and has a great feel to it. Battery life with the 6 cell and browsing the internet is around 16 hours with BSPWM as my WM (though I haven't timed it precisely) ACPI is reporting 60% left on my 6 cell and it is estimating 10hrs remaining and 100% on my internal battery so it may be a bit longer.

The screen has done me well. Can sit outside and see just fine as long as it's not in direct sunlight. The colors are pretty acurate and aren't washed out. The laptop has more than excess of power and RAM for my non-gaming needs. I'm barely pushing this thing at all unless compiling packages. I'm planning on upgrading the HDD to SSD next year after Samsung announces their new 2.5" SSDs and hopefully putting a 2tb SSD or more in it to last for the Thinkpad's life for various media for travelling and reliability.

I have a few complaints about the device though.

  • The plastic has starting creaking randomly, and will do so far a few days at random spots. Then after some finiking to get rid of it, it'll go away

  • No HDMI out which make more sense than Display Port provided IMO

  • The clips holding the back panel on

  • 42mm m.2 slot as it is SATA based instead of PCIe and 80mm

Other than those small complaints, I'll be holding onto this laptop for quite a while.
